What comes up in Erina

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. Treat the rows as the usual shape of the job locally. A specific property can differ, and that is what a site visit settles.

Internal strip out ahead of a new tenancy

Walls, ceilings, linings and fit out out of a building that stays standing.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, structural elements identified, then removal by hand so nothing retained is disturbed.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant, material carried out and loaded at the kerb.

Commercial building demolition

Shopfronts and light industrial premises where the slab and hardstand are part of the job.

How it is handled
Survey, disconnections, soft strip, then the structure with steel and clean concrete separated as it comes down.
What does it
Large excavator with a grapple, hammer for the slab, truck and dogs.

Internal strip outs and partial removal

Walls, floors, linings and fit out taken out of a building that stays standing, usually ahead of a renovation rather than a rebuild.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, then the removal done by hand so that what remains is not disturbed. Structural elements are identified before anything is cut.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant only, with material carried out and loaded at the kerb.

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Commercial and light industrial alongside residential So the work ranges from shopfronts and tenancies to ordinary knockdowns.
  • Internal strip outs A regular job here, where the building stays and the fit out comes out ahead of a new tenancy.
  • Hidden material in commercial interiors Flues, switchboard backing, fire doors and vinyl tile adhesive rather than the obvious places.
  • Better truck access than the beachside suburbs Which helps the cartage considerably.

Erina has wide commercial truck access for this part of the coast, with commercial streets built for heavy vehicles. The planning effort usually goes into working alongside tenancies that stay open rather than into getting plant onto the site.

Erina questions

What people ask before we start

Can you strip out a tenancy while the others keep trading?
Yes, and it is common here. It means hoarding, dust and noise control, agreed hours and a sequence that keeps the neighbouring access open throughout.
Where does asbestos turn up in commercial buildings?
Rarely where people look first. Flues, switchboard backing boards, fire doors, pipe insulation and vinyl tiles with bitumen adhesive are the usual places, which is why the whole building is surveyed before a scope is written.
Does sandy ground change how an excavation is done?
Yes. Sandy material drains well and batters poorly, so a face that has to stand is battered back or supported rather than left vertical, and near the water the water table is close enough that dewatering is planned rather than discovered.
Is the asbestos removal a separate engagement?
A separate licence, but not a separate engagement. Licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal and an independent licensed assessor issues the clearance, while Max holds demolition licence AD214737 and runs the programme across all of it.
